items.title: Ireland had not already won or swept the series
items.finding: The historical prediction says Ireland had already won the Namibia series and could complete a sweep. Cricket Ireland's 24 October report says Namibia won the second ODI by 31 runs to level the five-match series 1–1. The third ODI is not the end of that tour.
items.action: Correct or withdraw the claim and reconsider the selection; do not infer a winner.

items.title: Incorrect player age
items.finding: The historical text describes Lilli Tagger as 22. Her WTA biography gives her date of birth as 17 February 2008, so she was 18 on 27 October 2026. The Guangzhou draw separately lists her against Venus Williams.
items.action: Correct the age and reassess the remainder of the text independently.

items.title: Favourite assigned to the wrong team
items.finding: The historical Boston–Carolina totals prediction calls Boston the −192 to −196 favourite. In the NHL feed for game 2026020189, those named partner prices are listed for Carolina; Boston is listed at +158 or +160.
items.action: Correct the attribution and check the totals argument separately; a moneyline is not a totals estimate.

items.title: An unannounced XI was stated as certain
items.finding: The historical India prediction states that Ishan Kishan's injury keeps Vaibhav Sooryavanshi in the XI. The Cricket Australia match centre showed both teams as 'Team to be announced' at this review. An earlier appearance does not establish the future starting XI.
items.action: Do not state a future XI until an appropriate official team announcement is available.

items.title: Qualifier wording conflicts with the entry designation
items.finding: The Fernandez–Sakatsume text suggests that Sakatsume had to come through qualifying to be in Tokyo. The WTA's singles draw marks her 'WC' (wildcard), not 'Q' (qualifier).
items.action: Correct the entry description rather than attributing qualification to the player.

items.title: Opposite-sign prices described as effectively the same
items.finding: The historical Philadelphia prediction calls an originated −120 essentially the same as NHL partner quotes of +104 to +106. Their raw break-even rates are about 54.5% and 49.0%–48.5%, respectively; those are materially different, before considering margins or settlement rules.
items.action: Describe the prices distinctly and avoid claiming no gap without a valid like-for-like comparison.

items.title: Fair-price and margin-loaded price window mismatch
items.finding: The inspected originator marks in-window using fair_american, although its documentation says it gates the margin-loaded price. Three archived picks have in_window=true but margin-loaded prices below −250: Kalpa −259, Fernandez −269 and Eire Og +0.5 −291. The archived fair lines are −225, −233 and −250, respectively.
items.action: Define whether the user window applies to the offered or fair price, test each displayed price consistently, and never clamp a price to the boundary.

items.title: Tip popularity is not demonstrated predictive calibration
items.finding: The inspected originator applies a Dirichlet shrinkage formula to counts of OLBG tips and presents the result as a win chance. That calculation is reproducible as a smoothed selection share, but no out-of-sample calibration establishing it as a sporting win probability was recorded in the inspected pick payload. An official fixture match alone does not supply that calibration.
items.action: Separate consensus from independent probability and withhold confidence or fair-value claims until documented, time-correct validation is available.

items.title: Opposing sides presented together without a portfolio explanation
items.finding: The inspected pick list contains both Milwaukee and Tampa Bay moneylines for the same game, and both Milwaukee −1.5 and Tampa Bay +1.5 run lines. These are opposing outcomes within each of those markets; the public list does not explain a hedge or a coherent stake plan.
items.action: Do not present both sides as independent recommendations without explicit settlement and portfolio rationale.

items.title: No-bet notes counted on the picks page
items.finding: Several entries included in the historical pick count explicitly say they are placeholders or not recommendations, including Stewart Cink, Wyndham Clark and Penrith's outright. Their presence in a pick total can make the quota look closer than it is.
items.action: Separate research-only notes from actionable, fully sourced written predictions.

items.title: Test-match date needs an event-start cross-check
items.finding: The historical OLBG inventory labels South Africa–Australia 31 October. Cricket Australia describes the third Test as 27–31 October and states that the first ball is on 27 October. The OLBG label must not automatically be treated as the first ball without understanding the market's own timestamp.
items.action: Keep the two source dates distinct; do not promote a pre-match selection once play has started.

items.title: Tournament-end label is not a verified start time
items.finding: The OLBG listing shows 1 November for the Maybank Championship, while LPGA describes the tournament as 29 October–1 November. The last date in a multi-day event cannot safely stand in for its start or for a pre-event market deadline.
items.action: Store the governing body's event start separately from the market's timestamp and re-check availability.

items.title: Blank probable pitcher does not prove a bullpen plan
items.finding: The historical Milwaukee text refers to a probable bullpen game. The MLB feed names Tampa Bay's Griffin Jax as probable but has no probablePitcher object for Milwaukee at this check. A missing starter entry does not itself establish either a bullpen plan or an injury.
items.action: Leave the Brewers' starter and usage plan unconfirmed until supported by an explicit official announcement.

items.title: Previously missing official volleyball fixture references located
items.finding: The historical volleyball notes state that the Italian league fixture sources were not opened. The league's preview now supplies a direct reference to both Marignano–Bergamo and Conegliano–Vallefoglia. This resolves the limited question of event identity, not a betting price or player availability.
items.action: Use the exact league pages for identity; separately review form, injuries, live market, independent probability and prose.

items.title: PR #37: an edge over a de-vigged benchmark is not necessarily an edge at the offered price
items.finding: In the separate PR #37 snapshot at 19b53ff, Hye Jin Choi is shown at +1000 (decimal 11.00) with an estimated win chance of 8.31%. Under simple win/loss settlement with no pushes or each-way terms, that implies −8.59% expected net per unit, although the text cites a positive edge against the de-vigged benchmark. Wyndham Clark at +1000 and 7.90% similarly implies −13.10%. These are dated snapshot prices, not current offers.
items.action: Compare the proposed probability with the actual selection price and correct settlement terms before calling anything a betting edge.

items.title: PR #37: podium Yes outcomes are not mutually exclusive
items.finding: The PR #37 snapshot prices the Mexico City Grand Prix podium Yes selections as if exactly one driver could satisfy the market. Multiple drivers can finish on the podium, so normalizing all drivers’ individual Yes probabilities to 100% is not the same as removing margin from a mutually exclusive win market. The displayed Leclerc example has +110 (decimal 2.10) and an estimated 15.73% fair chance.
items.action: Price each driver’s Yes/No market with matching settlement data, or use a joint finishing-order method; leave it unpriced if the needed inputs are missing.

items.title: PR #37: volleyball set score mislabelled as player performance
items.finding: The PR #37 snapshot labels several volleyball Set Score selections with family “player” and describes the outcome as a player-performance market. A 3–2 or 3–0 set score describes the result of the match, not an individual player prop.
items.action: Classify and price set-score outcomes by their actual mutually exclusive match settlement; recheck the affected prose.

items.title: PR #37: generic official directories do not establish every event
items.finding: In the PR #37 snapshot at 19b53ff, 38 of 63 picks have official_level=directory, 22 have competition, and 3 have event; 37 explicitly have official_support=false. The price calculation blends de-vigged OLBG prices and tip-share counts. A link to a governing body does not establish every event-specific fact, availability field or out-of-sample probability calibration.
items.action: Describe the estimates as market-derived research until event-level facts, availability and independent calibration are captured; do not equate link presence with confirmation.
